clue.text: Learn about the shrub found on moorland

indicators.note: about means one word goes around another, so the word for learn wraps the clue's own 'the'

parts.note: to learn of news is to hear it

explanation.surface: A nature lesson about a moorland shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is the purple-flowered ling that covers British upland moors.

clue.text: Owns snowmobile, yet appears stressed

parts.note: to own is to have, so owns gives has
a sled is a vehicle for travelling over snow

explanation.surface: A snowmobile owner still looks harassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassled means harassed and under pressure.

clue.text: Saw a team gain meritorious award

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone saw a sports side receive an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning a saying. XI is a team of eleven; OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a maxim, a self-evident truth.

clue.text: Alluring lady appears at one o'clock

parts.note: o'clock tells the hour of the day
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seductive woman turns up at 1pm.
explanation.walkthrough: One o'clock is the first hour, so read it as HOUR I, with the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is a beautiful maiden of Islamic paradise, used of any seductive woman.

clue.text: A random error by manual worker

indicators.note: an error means the letters have gone wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A labourer makes a mistake by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges A and RANDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadman is a labourer who builds or repairs roads.

clue.text: Self-satisfied bounder or bullish opponent

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword slang for sanctimonious or smug
a bounder is an old-fashioned word for a cad, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Either a smug rotter or someone who stands against the bulls of the stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bullish' looks like stock-market talk but means 'against a bull' literally; PI is pious, BOUNDER is British slang for a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the horseman in a bullfight who goads the animal with a lance.

clue.text: Forecast made before the age of enlightenment?

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before
a sage is a wise person, one who has reached enlightenment

explanation.surface: A prophecy made before the eighteenth-century era of reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made before' looks like 'earlier than', but it gives PRE; the Age of Enlightenment is the 18th-century movement, read here as the age at which one becomes a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or be a sign of a future event.

clue.text: Ring one gent to cancel engagement

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
I is the Roman numeral for one
a toff is British slang for an upper-class gentleman

explanation.surface: Phoning a gentleman to break off a betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To call it off is to abandon a plan, here an engagement to marry.

clue.text: Hedonists turned out to be deceptive

indicators.note: turned out means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Pleasure-seekers prove to be liars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges HEDONISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest means untruthful, intending to mislead.

clue.text: Surrender and negotiate again

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again
to treat with someone is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: Giving up and reopening talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrender' stretches a little: to retreat is to give ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw or give ground in the face of an enemy.

clue.text: Demand that I put slate elsewhere

indicators.note: elsewhere tells us the letters of these words are put in another place, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone insists that the roofing slate be moved to another spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elsewhere' rearranges the letters of I, PUT and SLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipulate is to require something as a condition of an agreement.

clue.text: Heard record of his musical works

indicators.note: heard means the word we want sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: a list is a written record of items

explanation.surface: Someone listened to a recording of a composer's pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' signals a sound-alike: LIST (record) said out loud gives the Hungarian composer's name. A composer's name stands for his works, as in 'playing Liszt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer's surname is used for his compositions, so the Hungarian pianist's name means his output.

clue.text: Religion means graduate is immersed in lamentations

indicators.note: immersed in means these pieces are sunk inside the abbreviation of the book

parts.note: LAM is the standard abbreviation of Lamentations, a book of the Old Testament
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: Some faith's teaching includes a graduate's study of mournful laments.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamentations is the Old Testament book, abbreviated in Bible references; 'means' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamaism is the Tibetan form of Buddhism, led by lamas.

clue.text: Such fatty tissue made OAPs die

indicators.note: made here means the letters are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim claim that fat killed off some pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges OAPS and DIE. OAP (old-age pensioner) is British for a retired person. The answer names the kind of tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes animal fat stored in the body, the kind found in fatty tissue.

clue.text: Many a union results from flirtation

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, hence many
an alliance is a union of partners

explanation.surface: Lots of marriages begin with flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a crossword stand-in for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic involvement, light amorous play.

clue.text: Nothing in Hercules' disposition was lewd

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the rearranged hero's name
disposition, an arrangement, signals the letters are disposed afresh

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: The hero Hercules had a lustful nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' rearranges HERCULES to LECHERUS; 'in' puts O (nothing) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous means given to lust, sexually depraved.

clue.text: Entre nous, it's popular with Tommy

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Tommy Atkins was the generic name for a British private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier speaks confidentially about being well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Entre nous is French for between ourselves, confidentially.

clue.text: Open on time

parts.note: on and over are both prepositions meaning above or upon
T is the abbreviation for time in physics

explanation.surface: A shop sign saying it opens punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden or secret.

clue.text: He steps back to make a summary

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a man who steps in the reverse direction

parts.note: a pacer is one who paces, stepping to and fro

explanation.surface: A man retraces his steps to produce a brief review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses PACER, one who paces (steps).
explanation.definitionFit: A recap, short for recapitulation, is a brief restatement of the main points.

clue.text: Chorus keeps Italian monk in check

indicators.note: in places the friar's title inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
Fra is the Italian title for a friar or monk

explanation.surface: A choir holds back a singing Italian friar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' is just a link here; the container signal is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is the repeated chorus of a song.

clue.text: Keep healthy in poverty to become advantaged

parts.note: to keep healthy is to be fit, giving BE

indicators.note: in places the second word of the phrase inside the word for poverty

parts.note: need is the state of lacking money, poverty
the second half of the phrase be fit gives FIT

explanation.surface: Staying well despite being poor turns out to be an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-word phrase 'keep healthy' splits in two: its first word stands in front, and 'in' slips its second word inside the word for poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Benefited means gained or profited, having had an advantage.

clue.text: Salvo to honour VIP?

explanation.surface: Guns fired in tribute to a dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial gunfire salute is a large shot; a very important person is a prominent figure.

clue.text: No Frenchman in Alabama is titled

parts.note: M is short for monsieur, a Frenchman
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: No French visitor lives in an American southern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container here: it is spelt out as IN in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means existing in name only, as a title holder without real power.

clue.text: Ill-natured old comedian

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the letters are put together badly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumpy veteran comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill' rearranges NATURED. Jimmy Durante was a big-nosed American comedian and singer of the mid-twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Durante was an American comic entertainer famous for his large nose.

clue.text: Touching display of emotion

explanation.surface: A moving outpouring of sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means moving or tender; as a noun it is an emotion shown or sensed.

clue.text: Grumble, and get mum down

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, mum
down and under both mean below

explanation.surface: Someone complains and makes their mother feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get mum down' reads as depressing her, but it is a plain charade, mother on top of the word for below.
explanation.definitionFit: To maunder is to talk or complain in a rambling, moaning way.

clue.text: Disquieted, but not down-cast

parts.note: the opposite of down is up
to cast metal is to set it in a mould

explanation.surface: Unsettled though not depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down-cast' looks like the word for sad; split it at the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset means troubled and agitated.

clue.text: Senior 'tec harboured stolen loincloth

indicators.note: harboured means the detective holds the word for stolen inside

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a senior police detective
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A police inspector concealed a stolen garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tec is old slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a long cloth worn round the waist by Hindu men.

clue.text: Greek market for silver or aluminium initially

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, from Latin argentum

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the metal named

explanation.surface: Trading metals for cash in an ancient bazaar.
explanation.walkthrough: AG is silver's chemical symbol; 'initially' picks the first letter of 'aluminium'.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the open marketplace and assembly area of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Common teaching command delivered with ease

explanation.surface: A teacher's instruction given effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher tells pupils to lower raised arms; idiomatically it also means winning easily, as a jockey with lowered reins.

clue.text: Name a perfume about to be produced

parts.note: a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: Christening a new fragrance ahead of its launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, emerging.

clue.text: Sober individual put in ornamental fabric by window

indicators.note: put in means these pieces go inside the word for the fabric

parts.note: lace is a delicate decorative openwork fabric
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol
I is a single individual, the first-person one

explanation.surface: A teetotaller hangs lace curtains by a window.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, teetotal, is the crossword's usual abstainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice window has small diamond panes set in a crisscross of lead strips.
